stories.title: Stranger Anonymously Pays $420 Lunch Tab for 27 Disabled Residents and Caregivers
stories.label: people
stories.summary: A group of 27 people from a disability community center in Incheon, South Korea, stopped for a barbecue lunch together, just like any other outing. When it came time to pay, the staff told them someone they'd never met had already covered the entire $420 bill and asked to stay anonymous. The quiet generosity left the group, who care for and support disabled residents every day, feeling seen and appreciated. It's a small reminder that kindness between strangers still happens every day, no strings attached.
stories.why_good: A real act of anonymous generosity that happened and brightened the day of a group of caregivers and the people they support, with no suffering or conflict at its center.

stories.title: Divers Rescue Kangaroo Stranded Over a Mile Out at Sea
stories.label: animals
stories.summary: A young kangaroo somehow ended up swimming a mile and a half out in the ocean off South Australia's Boston Bay. A boat captain spotted the little guy paddling along, clearly exhausted and way out of his depth, literally. A scuba diver and his crew jumped into action and carefully guided the roo back toward shore to safety. It's the kind of wonderfully odd, only-in-Australia rescue that ends with everyone, including the kangaroo, getting to go home. No drama, no disaster, just neighbors (and a diver) looking out for a lost critter.
stories.why_good: A real, completed rescue of an animal in a strange predicament, with a clean happy ending and no underlying tragedy.
